question.text: Ms. Shruti Verma, a prospective LP, asks whether SEBI has 'approved' the PPM of 'Kaveri Delta Fund'. As the manager, what is the accurate response?

answer.text: Yes, SEBI approves every PPM before the scheme can be launched
SEBI provides only observations on the PPM; it does not approve the document, and the manager bears responsibility for the accuracy of disclosures
SEBI approves the PPM only after the fund reaches first close
SEBI approves the PPM but the approval is subject to material change in strategy

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 13.5, SEBI provides only observations on the PPM submitted to them and does not approve the document. The chapter quotes SEBI's standard disclaimer: 'submission of the PPM to SEBI should not in any way be deemed or construed that the same has been cleared or approved by SEBI'. It is the Manager's responsibility to ensure the PPM is true, accurate, and in compliance with AIF Regulations. The Trap: Many LPs assume SEBI filing = SEBI approval. This is a crucial investor-education point. Approval concept applies to public-market offer documents (DRHP/RHP), not AIF PPMs. Cross-Exam Context: Contrast with NISM-V-A (mutual funds) where SID/KIM are registered but similarly not 'approved'. In XIX-C manager exam this distinction matters for disclaimers in LP communications. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always include the SEBI disclaimer verbatim in your investor deck footer — prevents mis-selling allegations and aligns with the standard text SEBI shares with AIFs.
